newsitem.title: FRANCE: Noyer says France, Germany on same growth trend.
newsitem.headline: Noyer says France, Germany on same growth trend.

text.p: There is no disparity between economic growth in France and Germany, a top aide to Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Thursday.

Christian Noyer, head of Arthuis's private office, said France and Germany both had 0.7 percent growth over the whole of the first half, which if this carried on for the whole year would give growth of around 1.5 percent.
"The question is to know whether we are still on a growth trend of 1.5 to two percent, or if there there will be stronger growth of two and a half to three percent," Noyer said.
Reuters earlier incorrectly reported that Noyer had said France and Germany would have growth next year of 2.5 to three percent. Noyer made no forecast for 1997 growth.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis has said French growth next year is likely to be between 2.25 to 2.5 percent, slightly lower than the 2.8 percent forecast for 1997 earlier this year.
Germany earlier reported a strong rise in second quarter GDP after a shrinkage in the first quarter. France in contrast had a sharp rebound in the first quarter and downturn in the second.

"There is no decoupling of the economies in our two countries. Developments in Germany are extremely close to those in ours. GDP growth in France and Germany in the first half is exactly the same, 0.7 percent," Noyer said.
"We will continue to have an evolution that is totally parallel," he said.
